body: Montenegro uses standard European licence plates with a distinctive red circle containing the coat of arms, which is visible even when blurred. This distinguishes them from Albanian plates.
Montenegro is a small, mountainous country with lush green inland mountains and exposed rock on coastal mountains. Roads are typically narrow.
The most common bollard in Montenegro is white with a black top, a red front reflector, and a white back reflector. These bollards are also found in Slovenia.
Montenegro uses either black-on-white or red-on-yellow chevrons.
Guardrails in Montenegro are often rusted.
Montenegro is unique in the Balkans for commonly using both A-type and B-type guardrails.
Montenegro uses simple round concrete or wooden poles.
Rifts in the sky, caused by poor camera stitching, are a common meta for Montenegro, especially inland. This is also common in Albania.
Street View coverage in Montenegro is limited to main roads, with very few minor roads being covered.
Montenegro coverage can be split into two types: coastal areas have a short antenna and no rifts, while inland areas have a long antenna with frequent rifts.
The north of Montenegro often features green, agricultural valleys and deforested hills.
The Bay of Kotor area is touristy and populated, characterized by a distinct steep, rocky ridge along the water.
The area around and south of Podgorica has dry, treeless mountains and is also known for its vineyards.
Pine forests are most common in the east of Montenegro.
Durmitor National Park has a unique landscape of grassy, treeless, high-altitude mountains. The town of Žabljak within the park has distinctive architecture.
Podgorica, the capital, is Montenegro's largest city and is identifiable by its modern buildings and infrastructure.
The Cemi River Valley features distinctive staircase-like mountainsides.
Slansko Lake is recognizable by the many small islands within it.
The Pljevlja Coal Mine is identifiable by a large, artificial wall of gravel that is often visible from a distance.
On road P15, the Google Car can be seen following a police car.
The southern part of the E80 road features distinctive yellow outer lines.
The Skadar Lake Bridge is recognizable by the adjacent railway track and stone bollards.
